Thanks for looping me in. A few technical notes to set expectations:

- Dedicated expansion: we can provision an additional 8x H100-style GPUs into a dedicated reserved pool in the same region by 2027-07-01 if we sign the amendment by 2027-05-10. Lead time is mainly allocation and OS image prep.

- Throughput guarantee: we can offer a regional SLO for sustained throughput, but it depends on model family + quantization. For Llama2-70B-class equivalent, 6k tokens/s sustained across the pool is reasonable with the added GPUs and optimized batching. We will include a per-route throughput SLA in the appendix.

- Burst/overflow options (tradeoffs):
  1) On-demand hosted spillover (recommended for flexibility): requests exceeding dedicated capacity route to Redwood hosted capacity. Pros: no hard cap on availability during spikes; Cons: ~15–30% higher per-token cost during spillover and slightly higher 50–90 p50/p90 latency depending on model and region.
  2) Hard cap / reject policy: once reserved capacity is saturated, excess requests are throttled/rejected. Pros: predictable cost (no overspend) and bounded latency; Cons: potential dropped requests or queuing on the customer side — customers must implement retry/backoff.
  3) Hybrid gating (preferred for renewal deals): allow spillover up to a configurable compute budget (e.g., X GPU-hours or $Y) per billing month; beyond that, enter hard cap. This gives a predictable spend collar while retaining resiliency.

- Metering & reporting: we'll provide token-level and GPU-hour dashboards per month, plus a realtime alert if spillover usage approaches 80% of the agreed monthly spill budget.

I recommend the hybrid gating: we'll propose a default monthly spill budget (e.g., 300 GPU-hours) and an overage rate; procurement can pick a monetary ceiling if they prefer.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Sanjay — answering procurement bullets and next steps:

- Pricing: Draft numbers in attached appendix (Catalyst-Capacity-Appendix-v3.pdf) — shows 12-month reserved pricing with a per-month line item for 8x H100-equivalent GPUs and a recommended monthly spill budget priced at $28k/month (equivalent to ~320 GPU-hours at the proposed overage rate). We can lower the spill spend if you prefer a tighter collar.

- SLA wording: we can include the legal-friendly line you requested. For operational clarity we add a note that the 50ms metric applies during common-case region and model parity; the SLA also calls out force majeure and cross-region reroutes as exceptions.

- Pre-warm option: Yes — we can provide a warm-host pool in the hosted fleet and preferential routing to that pool while on spillover. There is a small additional warm-hosting fee (listed in the appendix). Pre-warm reduces the cold-start latency component and narrows p95/p99 deltas.

Next steps: Jasmine — can you send a renewal amendment PDF and the redline doc? I'll draft the procurement-friendly exhibit and include the hybrid gating defaults. If Catalyst signs the 12-month amendment by 2027-05-10 we can hit the July 1 start.

Thanks,
